findings.title: Default-strategy upgrade tests never enable rolling-updates
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when the parameterized strategy is null, so the new spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates] setup never runs for that case. testImageChange(null) and testCacheMaxCount(null) still deploy that CR and expect a successful recreate or rolling upgrade. The operator guide added in this PR says the operator fails unless the preview feature is enabled, including for the default (unset) strategy. As written, those two cases either time out or fail reconciliation, or they pass only because the feature is not actually required and the new caution is wrong. Enable the feature for every deployment this class creates (and append it to any features already on the CR instead of replacing the enabled list), or narrow the caution so it does not claim the operator fails for the legacy default strategy.

findings.title: Exit code 4 reused for a different outcome
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, and the new feature-disabled path exits 4. Until this commit the compatibility CLI returned 4 when a rolling upgrade was not possible. No operator upgrade source is updated in this PR, and the distribution tests only assert stderr text, not the numeric code. A caller that still treats 4 as recreate (the previous behavior, and the code the operator would have been written against) will scale the StatefulSet down when the preview feature is simply off, which is the default. A caller updated only to the documented recreate code 3 will treat the new 4 as an unexpected error and abort the upgrade. Do not reuse the old recreate code: keep 4 as recreate (it does not collide with picocli 1 and 2) and use a new code for feature-disabled, and assert both codes in UpdateCommandDistTest.

findings.title: New exit code 4 and recreate code 3 are not asserted
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks that stderr contains the disabled-feature sentence. It does not assert exit code 4, and it only launches the metadata subcommand, not update-compatibility check, which is the command whose exit code the guide tells automation to branch on. testWrongVersions still only checks the incompatibility message after RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3, so a process that still exits 4 (or 1) for an incompatible metadata file would pass. Assert exit code 4 for both subcommands when the feature is off, and assert exit code 3 for the incompatible-version check.
